correctness.rationale: Every global alphabet renaming orbit has one restricted-growth representative. For each prefix i and candidate border k, the abelian condition is equality of three symbol-count differences; the 4-bit-per-entry encoding is injective up to n=16. Independent C++17 exhaustive enumeration over all 3^15 words with first symbol 0 (different from canonical restricted-growth enumeration), division by two for nonconstant relabeling classes and direct prefix-count checks recovered all 16 rows including 1151825 at n16; its complete 353-level n16 histogram matched the committed CSV byte for byte, including SHA-256 6cd4f6d044008762b8bba80e45ad656d7de02b9eb3d5c2539fe64348157ed3b1. For the infinite extremal claim, b_i=i-1 iff w_i=w_1, so an array fixes exactly which later positions repeat the first letter; any nonzero array fixes at least one such position, leaving at most two choices per other position, giving at most 3*2^(n-2) labeled words, versus 3*2^(n-1) for all zero. Canonical class count follows after fixing first 0 and factoring symbol permutation. Finite exhaustiveness is not extrapolated beyond n16.
